history.period: Medieval Datta Kshetra; shrine tradition built up over centuries after Nrusinha Saraswati's stay (15th century)
history.summary: IDENTITY NOTE: there is no famous 'Dattatreya Temple' in Sangli city proper; the most likely referent of the CSV row is the famous Shri Kshetra Audumbar Dattatreya temple in Palus taluka, Sangli district (~26 km from Sangli city), on the bank of the Krishna river. Per the Shri Guru Charitra, Shri Nrusinha Saraswati, the second incarnation of Dattatreya, came to Audumbar after his pilgrimage and performed Chaturmas anushtaan (the four holy months) here in secret. A dull-witted Brahmin boy, advised by goddess Bhuvaneshwari (whose temple is on the opposite bank), fell at the sage's feet and was blessed with scholarship — thereafter thousands flocked for darshan, and when the sage left he left his padukas under the audumbar tree, over which a devotee from Poona erected a small shrine and built a dharmashala. The swayambhu paduka of Lord Dattatreya is the main object of worship; the temple is built in North Indian style with a recent outer mandap, commanding a view of the Krishna. The sage Brahmanand of Girnar later discovered and popularised the kshetra. Devotees rank Audumbar with Ganagapur and Narsobawadi among the great Datta places. Nearby: Bhuvaneshwari Temple across the river, Brahmanand Swami Math, and the Sangameshwar Shiva Temple at Haripur. The CSV town 'Sangli' is approximate; the actual village is Audumbar, 8 km east of Bhilawadi railway station.

name: Dattatreya Temple, Audumbar (Shri Kshetra Audumbar)
town_description: Audumbar (Shri Kshetra Audumbar) is a village and Datta Kshetra in Palus taluka, Sangli district, Maharashtra, on the bank of the Krishna river, about 12 km from Palus, 8 km east of Bhilawadi railway station and about 26 km from Sangli city.

travel.railway: Bhilawadi railway station (~8 km); Sangli railway station (~26 km)
travel.road: Audumbar is reachable by road from Palus (~12 km) and Sangli (~26 km); autos and private cars available

visitor_information.best_time: October-March; Dattatreya Jayanti is the main festival
visitor_information.opening_hours: Official visiting hours not published - verify locally before visiting
